uncited: A technique to fix 'cracks' (holes/slots) in voxelization caused by steep primitive slopes relative to the view direction.
Swizzle the X, Y, and Z components of the vertex positions in the Geometry Shader to change the projection direction.
Crack Condition: If $|ddx(depth)| > 1.0$ or $|ddy(depth)| > 1.0$, cracks occur perpendicular to the depth direction.

Key developments include using simplified meshes for obstacles to allow voxelization at every frame with little performance cost [S1, unofficial], distributing workload between CPU and GPU for ROI computation and rasterization to handle complex models efficiently [S2, unofficial], and fixing cracks caused by steep primitive slopes via axis swizzling in the Geometry Shader [S3, unofficial].

The claim accurately reflects the content of the provided sources. Source [S1] explicitly states that using simplified meshes (low level of detail) allows voxelization at every frame with little performance cost. Source [S2] describes a pipeline architecture that distributes workload between CPU (ROI computation, classification) and GPU (rasterization) to handle models efficiently. Source [S3] details a technique using axis swizzling in the Geometry Shader to select projection directions based on face normals to fix cracks caused by steep primitive slopes (high depth gradients).
